observations.finding: 1 of 50 pathways significant at BH-q<0.05; top pathway HALLMARK_CHOLESTEROL_HOMEOSTASIS SMD=0.82 up, q=0.016; set median 0.334 vs rest 0.316; availability 27 vs 76.
PBRM1 mutation frequency 74.1% vs 25.0%, delta=0.491, OR=8.57 (95% CI 3.14-23.42), Fisher p=1.5e-05, q=0.00033; set 20/27 vs rest 19/76.
No CNV features significant at q<0.05; top continuous chr9q Cliff's delta=-0.375 (q=0.204); top gain/loss PTEN loss freq 25.9% vs 5.3%, OR=6.3 (95% CI 1.68-23.69), q=0.204.

biological_support.statistical_interpretation: RNA shows a single significant pathway with moderate effect size (SMD 0.82) and low FDR, but the remaining pathways are not significant. WXS shows a strong, significant PBRM1 enrichment with large effect and narrow CI, surviving multiple-testing correction. CNV shows no significant features; the top CNV trends (e.g., PTEN loss, chr9 loss) have moderate effect sizes but wide CIs and q>0.2, indicating weak evidence. Coherence across modalities is limited: RNA and CNV provide only weak signals, while WXS provides strong support.
biological_support.medical_interpretation: The set is characterized by a high frequency of PBRM1 mutations, a known ccRCC driver, and a modest cholesterol homeostasis transcriptional signature. CNV alterations are not statistically robust. These findings suggest a molecularly distinct subgroup with PBRM1 loss-of-function, but the overall biological support is driven primarily by mutation data.
limitations: RNA pathway analysis tested 50 pathways with only one significant; CNV analysis had no significant features after FDR.
Mutation analysis tested 22 genes; only PBRM1 remained significant after FDR.
Small set size (n=27) and multiple testing reduce power.
Clinical characterization was not used as molecular support.

cross_modal_consistency.statistical_interpretation: All modality median silhouettes are near zero, indicating that C0001 is not well separated from other sets in any single modality. biological_support.statistical_interpretation: RNA shows a strong, coherent pattern with 9 significant pathways, including up-regulation of pancreas beta cells, TGF-beta, and UV response, and down-regulation of allograft rejection, with q values as low as 0.008. WXS shows a suggestive PBRM1 enrichment but does not survive FDR (q=0.170). CNV shows two significant continuous features (chr12p and chr16p lower in set) with moderate-to-large effect sizes and q=0.027, but no significant gain/loss events. Coherence is moderate: RNA and CNV provide significant signals, while WXS is suggestive but not significant.
biological_support.medical_interpretation: The set exhibits a distinct transcriptional program with multiple significant pathways, and a CNV profile with lower copy number on chr12p and chr16p. PBRM1 mutations are enriched but not statistically robust after correction. These findings suggest a biologically distinct subgroup, but the evidence is not uniformly strong across modalities.
limitations: WXS PBRM1 enrichment does not survive FDR.
CNV gain/loss analysis had no significant features.
Small set size (n=18) and multiple testing reduce power.
RNA pathway results may be driven by a few samples.
